description: Turns an accepted Concept Card or Conception Brief into a component inventory and content-depth plan

evals.name: Step 1: Conception Brief branch
evals.prompt: plugin-planning's Step 1 is given $ARGUMENTS pointing at a file under .claude/output/plugin-conception/ -- a Conception Brief with Concept type = Enhance, targeting an existing skill. Which of Step 1's 3 branches applies, and what should plugin-planning do differently than if it had received a plain Concept Card?
evals.expected_output: The Conception Brief branch applies (not the Concept Card branch or the 'neither found' branch); plugin-planning reads the brief's existing baseline contract, implementation plan, and marketplace integration sections directly rather than re-deriving them, and runs only a shallow (repository-metadata depth) overlap re-check, not the exhaustive per-component search

evals.name: Step 1: Neither Concept Card nor Conception Brief found
evals.prompt: plugin-planning is invoked with $ARGUMENTS that doesn't resolve to any file under .claude/output/plugin-ideation/ or .claude/output/plugin-conception/ -- just a bare description like 'plan out a caching layer for skill X'. Which Step 1 branch applies and what happens next?
evals.expected_output: The 'neither found' branch applies; plugin-planning should not silently fabricate a Concept Card or Conception Brief -- it should either ask the user to run plugin-ideation/plugin-conception first, or explicitly state it's proceeding from the bare description with reduced upstream grounding
